newsitem.title: UK: Cox reports sharp rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Cox reports sharp rise in profits.

text.p: Lloyd's corporate vehicle Cox Insurance Holdings Plc on Thursday announced a sharp rise in annual profits helped by the acquisition of Christopherson Heath Group in October last year.
Pre-tax profits increased to 17.1 million stg for the year to March 31 compared with 1.3 million stg for the previous year.
Motor insurance company Christopherson Heath contributed 5.1 million stg of post acquisition profits.
The rise in profits included the receipt of 3.3 million stg of 1993 profit commission, delayed from 1996, due to the Lloyd's insurance market 'reconstruction and renewal' timetable.
By mid-morning Cox shares were 2-1/2 pence higher at 179 pence.
The acquisition of Christopherson Heath, one of the largest motor insurers in Lloyd's, has doubled the group's underwriting capacity to nearly 500 million stg.
In-house underwriting has increased to 134 million stg from 67 million stg.
Before the expenses of Names - the traditional backers of the Lloyd's market - profits from Cox managed syndicates rose to 76 million stg from 26 million stg.
Cox also acquired Groves, John & Westrup, a Liverpool-based specialist yacht and cargo insurer, in January 1997 and formed a Swedish underwriting company Cox Forsakring in September 1996.

The company which is currently proposing to amalgamate most of its London market syndicates into a single trading unit, said it believed it was well placed to take advantage of recent and future changes at Lloyd's.
